fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents appropriately avoid inventing database, API, deployment, testing or streaming experience. Python, Go and limited AWS exposure are presented honestly, but the material does not establish the core production-backend requirements. The recent coding slowdown is softened rather than explained, and useful transition, compensation and travel context is omitted.

issues: Only a first name is supplied; there is no email, telephone number or professional link. These details were not available in the source and should not have been invented.
Neither employment entry has a historical job title or full employment date range; only the Streamhaus departure date is given.
The source material is too sparse to establish seniority, duration of professional backend work or a meaningful employment history.
The headline emphasizes senior/staff targets rather than the advertised Backend Engineer title.
The third-person phrase 'the candidate’s primary cloud platform' is inappropriate for a personal CV.
The summary, skills and additional-information sections repeat the same few facts instead of providing distinct evidence.

reasons: The PDF extracts cleanly in a sensible single-column order with standard headings.
Most essential technical requirements are absent, and the source material does not support adding them.
Missing role titles and employment date ranges prevent reliable calculation of the required three years of experience.
There is no demonstrated relational-database, REST API, Docker, testing or CI/CD experience.

issues: The second paragraph repeats the internal-tools, dashboard, GCP and limited-AWS facts already stated rather than developing one concrete example.
It offers no evidence of backend-service ownership, measurable results or the core database/API requirements; those facts are also absent from the source.
The claim that pragmatic, sustainable engineering is a personal value is not grounded in the candidate material.
It misses the opportunity to explain the management-to-IC transition and level/compensation flexibility more convincingly.
The letter does not connect the candidate's travel capacity and remote preference to the advertised EU-remote route.
strengths: Names Tessel Cargo Software, the exact role and the Routing & Tracking team.
Correctly references dependable services, documentation, reliability work and concise design notes.
Does not pretend that GCP experience is deep AWS experience.
Concise, courteous and consistent with the CV's stated IC objective.

spacing_issues: Both documents occupy only the upper portion of their pages; the measurements report 51.8% fill for the CV and 44.3% for the letter.
The CV has a particularly large empty lower area, reinforcing how little employment evidence it contains.
consistency_issues: The CV's blue section rules run through the lower part of the heading lettering rather than sitting cleanly underneath.
The CV has a prominent centered name and subtitle, whereas the letter has no matching identity/contact header.
issues: The CV subtitle is long and visually crowded on one line.
Body text is legible at 11 pt and neither page shows text cutoff or overlapping body content.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'GCP is the candidate’s primary cloud platform' reads like an assessor's description rather than a candidate's CV.
'Go (rusty)' is candid but unnecessarily colloquial; 'Go — prior experience' would be more professional without implying current proficiency.

'I would bring my experience developing internal tools and cost-dashboard scripts, together with my GCP background and limited historical AWS exposure' repeats the preceding material and sounds labored.

notes_facts_used: Desire to return to hands-on senior/staff individual-contributor work rather than people management.
Recent internal-tool and cost-dashboard scripting work.
Fresh Python skills and rusty Go skills.
GCP as the main cloud platform.
Limited historical AWS exposure to EC2 and S3 at Nordfels.
Departure from Streamhaus in August 2026 after an organizational reorganization and merger.
notes_facts_ignored: Limited coding activity during the last two years beyond the stated tools and scripts.
Acceptance of lower compensation than a director role and a senior-engineer title.
Departure on good terms and availability of a reference.

evaluation.summary: The documents are readable, mostly faithful to the sparse notes and appropriately avoid inventing the many technical qualifications the job requires. However, the CV lacks contact details, historical job titles, employment ranges and evidence of production backend delivery, making an initial screening pass unlikely. The cover letter is company-specific but repetitive and does little to substantiate fit. Useful transition, compensation and travel context is omitted; although the separate preference field says none was given, the supplied notes explicitly state 'remote or hybrid in Munich,' which the outputs leave unaddressed.
